attributes.note: bacterial canker/black spot (angular, water-soaked, raised, vein-limited, chlorotic-halo)
anthracnose (irregular, dry, not raised/water-soaked, not strictly vein-angular)
anthracnose (discrete dark spots vs diffuse scorch)
sooty mould (BLACK, not white; older leaves; on honeydew)
early blight (coarser rings, lower-leaf-first, larger halos)

properties.pathogen_type: Fungus (superficial saprophyte/epiphyte, not a tissue pathogen)
properties.scientific_name: Capnodium spp. (e.g., C. mangiferae, C. ramosum) and allied fungi (Meliola, Tripospermum, Cladosporium)

synonyms: closely related to Tobacco mosaic virus (TMV)

properties.scientific_name: Xanthomonas spp. (four-taxon complex: X. euvesicatoria pv. euvesicatoria, X. euvesicatoria pv. perforans, X. hortorum pv. gardneri, X. vesicatoria)

properties.disease_progression: Young flush most susceptible: small dark spots, coalescence into irregular necrotic blotches, shot-hole, distortion; also blossom blight and postharvest fruit rot (not leaf-visible).
properties.taxonomy_note: A species complex; C. gloeosporioides is the classic name, with additional cryptic species regionally.

properties.common_name: Bacterial black spot / bacterial canker of mango
properties.disease_progression: Leaf lesions begin water-soaked, then raised, angular, black, vein-delimited lesions (often with a chlorotic halo), then older lesions dry to light-brown/ash-gray; also twig cankers and star-shaped gummy fruit lesions (not leaf-visible).
properties.taxonomy_note: MangoLeafBD label 'Bacterial Canker' is the same disease usually called bacterial black spot in the literature.

properties.disease_progression: Adults make scissor-like cuts on young leaves; cut/notched/trimmed margins and windowpane feeding scars; cut leaf tips drop; larvae feed between leaf surfaces.
properties.host_plant: Mango (especially nursery seedlings and young flush)
properties.taxonomy_note: Insect pest (beetle), NOT a pathogen. The class represents mechanical cutting/feeding damage. Use cutting/feeding vocabulary, never lesion/spot/infection.

properties.disease_progression: Twig/branch dieback from the tip downward; leaves on affected shoots yellow, brown, curl, and dry; defoliation; vascular discoloration in stems (not leaf-visible).
properties.taxonomy_note: Botryosphaeriaceae complex (chiefly Lasiodiplodia theobromae). As a MangoLeafBD leaf class it captures the leaf-level scorch of a twig/branch/tree-decline syndrome; captions describe only the leaf.

properties.disease_progression: Adult lays eggs in tender leaves; larvae feed inside; small raised wart-like galls form within ~a week; galls turn necrotic; premature leaf drop.
properties.taxonomy_note: Insect pest (fly), NOT a pathogen. The class represents larval-induced galls. Use gall/bump vocabulary, never flat lesion/spot.
No pathogen or pest. Young flush is normally coppery-red to pale/light-green (healthy, not disease).

properties.disease_progression: White superficial powdery growth on young leaves, inflorescences, and young fruit; leaf distortion; purplish-brown weathering; flower/fruit drop.
properties.taxonomy_note: Obligate biotroph, ectophytic; anamorph name Oidium mangiferae commonly used; teleomorph assignments vary in the literature.

properties.disease_progression: Honeydew deposits on the leaf; black superficial fungal colonization; black sooty coating over the (usually upper) leaf surface; shading reduces photosynthesis; the film flakes/peels when dry, revealing green tissue beneath.
properties.host_plant: Mango (surface only; indirect - follows sucking-insect infestation)
properties.pathogen_type: Fungus (superficial saprophyte/epiphyte, not a tissue pathogen)
properties.scientific_name: Capnodium spp. (e.g., C. mangiferae, C. ramosum) and allied fungi (Meliola, Tripospermum, Cladosporium)
properties.taxonomy_note: Superficial saprophyte/epiphyte growing on insect honeydew; the leaf tissue underneath is NOT infected. Use surface-coating vocabulary; never assert tissue necrosis.

properties.disease_progression: Seed/transplant-borne inoculum, then small water-soaked leaf spots, then dark angular necrotic lesions, then coalescence, blighting and defoliation.
properties.scientific_name: Xanthomonas spp. (four-taxon complex: X. euvesicatoria pv. euvesicatoria, X. euvesicatoria pv. perforans, X. hortorum pv. gardneri, X. vesicatoria)
properties.taxonomy_note: Species complex, repeatedly revised; PlantVillage label does not resolve species, so captions should stay at disease level and not name a species.

properties.disease_progression: Oldest/lowest leaves first, circular lesions enlarge with concentric rings, leaflet chlorosis, upward defoliation (also stem collar rot and fruit, not leaf-visible).
properties.taxonomy_note: Tomato-specialized Alternaria (A. linariae / A. tomatophila) sometimes distinguished from A. solani.

properties.disease_progression: Rapid: water-soaked leaf lesions, then large greasy blotches, then white underside sporulation, then whole-leaf and whole-plant collapse within days; petioles/stems affected.
properties.taxonomy_note: Oomycete (water mold), NOT a true fungus; family Peronosporaceae.

properties.disease_progression: Lower/older leaves first: pale diffuse upper patches with olive-to-brown velvety mold on underside; leaflets yellow, curl, wither, drop.
properties.taxonomy_note: Accepted name unsettled; Videira et al. 2017 adopt Fulvia fulva; some post-2017 work reverts to Cladosporium fulvum.

properties.disease_progression: Systemic: light/dark-green mosaic mottling, leaf distortion (fern-leaf), stunting; expression varies with strain, temperature, and light.
properties.host_plant: Tomato, tobacco, pepper, and many others
properties.taxonomy_note: Positive-sense ssRNA virus; family Virgaviridae, genus Tobamovirus. Expresses as systemic mottling/distortion, NOT discrete lesions.

properties.disease_progression: Lower/older leaves first: numerous small circular spots with dark margins and tan/gray centers, black pycnidia in centers, leaflet chlorosis, upward defoliation.
Fine stippling, then chlorotic/bronzed patches, then underside webbing, then desiccation/bronzing and leaf drop.
properties.host_plant: Very wide host range, including tomato
properties.taxonomy_note: Arthropod pest (mite), NOT a pathogen. The class represents feeding injury. Use pest/feeding-injury vocabulary, never infection/lesion/pathogen.

properties.disease_progression: Leaf spots, then lesions with subtle concentric rings and pale centers, then coalescence and blighting (also stem and sunken fruit lesions, not leaf-visible).
Systemic: new growth shows upward cupping/curling, marginal/interveinal yellowing, reduced leaflet size, stunting; flower drop.
properties.taxonomy_note: Single-stranded DNA virus; family Geminiviridae, genus Begomovirus. Whitefly-vectored. Expresses as cupping + yellowing + stunting, NOT lesions.

properties.canonical_label: a dry-weather disease (unlike anthracnose, not rain-driven)
entry through wounds (wind/sand abrasion) and stomata
explosive epidemics under cool wet conditions
extremely stable and persistent on surfaces/debris
favored by warm conditions and high whitefly populations
high humidity/dew during flowering and flush
high temperature (>27 c) and low humidity
important in florida and humid tropics
most important field/postharvest disease in humid tropics
opportunistic on stressed trees (drought, heat, wounds, pruning cuts)
outbreaks often follow broad-spectrum insecticide use
presence of honeydew-secreting insects (hoppers, scales, mealybugs, aphids)
rain, dew, and splashing spread conidia
spread by rain splash and wind
spread mechanically (handling, tools, contaminated seed, grafting)
survives on residue and weed hosts
transmitted by whitefly bemisia tabaci (persistent, circulative)
